messages:
alex: Customer reports duplicate charges when client retries POST on 429/timeouts. They say their SDK is defaulting retries. Anyone seen this pattern?
maria: Yep, we've seen it. Do we have repro steps or request/response headers?
alex: Repro steps from customer: send POST /v1/infer with body, network hiccup -> client sees timeout -> SDK auto-retries 3x -> server processed both requests. They do not send an Idempotency-Key. No Retry-After header in responses.
sam: Quick answers: SDK defaults are expo backoff + full jitter, max_retries=4 for older clients. That helps for transient network flakiness but unsafe for non-idempotent endpoints unless clients add idempotency keys.
maria: Can you paste the SDK config snippet to disable retries or set idempotency? I can forward to the customer.
sam: Sure. Example header approach (recommended):
```
Idempotency-Key: 1f7b9f2a-3d4c-4b1a-9e2f-3a8d9c0b2eee
```
Server should dedupe by that key for POST/charge-like ops.
To disable retries in client (JS SDK):
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ retry: { maxAttempts: 0 } });
```
Or explicitly set retry_policy: 'none' on per-call basis.
Also note: if the SDK retry happens after the server accepted the request but response was lost, idempotency is the only safe mitigation.

alex: Customer also asked if Redwood can return a Retry-After on rate limit responses so client backoffs more elegantly.
sam: We return Retry-After for strict rate-limit (HTTP 429 with rate_limit header) in most cases, but for intermittent downstream issues we sometimes return 503 without Retry-After. Recommend clients implement expo+jitter and honor Retry-After when present.
maria: For immediate mitigation I suggested: 1) Client add Idempotency-Key for write ops. 2) Set SDK maxAttempts=1 for this customer until they roll out keys. 3) We can suggest server-side dedupe if they can pass a unique request id.
infra-bot: [alert] spike detected: customer_x requests exceeded per-second quota at 2278501200. Auto-throttle engaged.
alex: That alert matches the customer's timeframe. Might explain the timeouts -> clients retried -> duplicate processing.
sam: Follow-up best practices to share with customer: short checklist
- Use Idempotency-Key on non-idempotent endpoints
- Respect Retry-After header and implement expo+jitter when absent
- Prefer client-side rate limiter to smooth bursts (token bucket)
- For SDK upgrades: move to latest which exposes per-call retry override

maria: I'm sending these steps and example curl repro + header snippet. Also offering a temporary quota bump while they implement keys.
alex: Thanks. I'll include the curl repro:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \ 
  --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 6
```
Simulate flaky network and watch for duplicated side-effects if no Idempotency-Key is set.
maria: Good. I'll mark this as support-escalated and follow up after they confirm keys rolled out. :thumbsup:
